answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by letting reputation decay, like a tide that slowly pulls standing back toward the ocean floor. Each identity earns weight only through verified good work, and that weight fades every epoch without fresh, attested contributions. A newcomer therefore starts near its nadir of influence and must keep working to rise, while an attacker who spins up thousands of fakes must continuously pay the cost of real, useful work for every one of them. Idle sock puppets sink, so maintaining a fake army costs more than any fraud it could win.
